title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Console Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Troubleshoots no-power, incomplete startup, or repeated boot interruption caused by external power, connections, accessories, controls, or environmental conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Surgical Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the CUSA Clarity while a patient depends on it for active surgical aspiration or tissue fragmentation. Notify the surgical team and transition to an approved alternate method or verified replacement system before removing the unit from clinical use. Inspect immediately for smoke, unusual odor, fluid intrusion, excessive heat, damaged power components, or visible electrical damage. If present, disconnect AC power when safe and remove the system from service. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely using an alternate method, and the console is available for controlled troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether the console was completely dead, powered briefly and shut down, froze during startup, restarted repeatedly, or reached a screen but would not become ready. Attempt startup only in a controlled environment without a patient connected. Observe indicator lights, display activity, fan noise, audible tones, and where the startup sequence stops. Expected outcome: The reported condition is reproduced or the console completes startup normally. If startup completes repeatedly without fault, continue with functional verification and troubleshooting may stop if no issue recurs.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is fully seated at the console and wall receptacle. Inspect the cord, plug, strain relief, and receptacle for damage or looseness. Verify the outlet using an appropriate electrical tester or known-good device. Avoid extension cords, damaged power strips, or questionable receptacles during testing. Expected outcome: Verified AC power is available and the console receives stable facility power. If correcting the outlet or connection restores reliable startup, perform final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Power Components
steps.instructions: Examine the console power inlet, cord connection, and accessible power controls for contamination, physical damage, or incomplete engagement. If an approved known-good compatible power cord is available, substitute it when appropriate. Expected outcome: External power components are intact and secure. A known-good cord either restores operation or rules out the detachable power cord as the cause.

steps.title: 5. Disconnect Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Power the unit off and disconnect nonessential external accessories that could complicate startup, while leaving only the connections necessary for basic console startup. Restart the console and compare behavior. Expected outcome: The console starts normally with nonessential accessories removed, or the startup problem remains independent of accessories. If one accessory causes the failure when reconnected, remove that accessory from use and stop troubleshooting after verification.

steps.title: 6. Check Controls and Physical Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible switches, touchscreen surfaces, connectors, vents, and the console housing. Confirm nothing is holding a control continuously activated and that the console is not obstructed or positioned where ventilation is restricted. Do not open the console or bypass protective circuitry. Expected outcome: No external obstruction, stuck control, or physical condition explains the startup issue.

steps.title: 7. Allow Environmental Conditions to Normalize
steps.instructions: If the console was recently moved from storage, exposed to unusual temperature conditions, or subjected to moisture, allow it to reach the appropriate clinical environment before another startup attempt. Do not operate equipment with suspected condensation or fluid intrusion. Expected outcome: The console starts normally after environmental conditions stabilize, or the startup problem persists.

steps.title: 8. Perform Repeated Controlled Startup Checks
steps.instructions: With verified AC power and approved external connections, perform controlled power cycles according to normal operating practice. Confirm the console consistently reaches its normal ready state without freezing, restarting, or shutting down. Expected outcome: The console reliably completes startup. If it does, proceed with applicable functional and electrical safety testing before return to service.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Reconnect the normal approved accessories needed for system testing and verify the console recognizes connected components, accepts controls, and remains stable during a nonclinical functional check. Complete electrical safety or other return-to-service testing required by facility policy and manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: The console starts reliably, remains powered, and passes required functional checks. Troubleshooting can stop and the device may be returned to service when all required testing passes.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If verified power, cord condition, connections, accessories, controls, and environment are satisfactory but the console still does not power on or complete startup, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The console is removed from service for qualified bench evaluation rather than subjected to unnecessary internal disassembly.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the CUSA Clarity console would not power on before a surgical case.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the detachable AC power cord was not fully seated at the console power inlet.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the power cord, verified repeated successful startups and normal functional operation, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the console was completely dead or partially started.
Point in startup where operation stopped.
Indicator lights or audible startup activity.
Evidence of heat, odor, fluid, or physical damage.
Final functional and electrical safety test status.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Handpiece Not Recognized or Will Not Tune
description: Addresses handpiece detection or tuning failures caused by connections, installation, accessories, contamination, handpiece condition, or incompatible setup.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Clinical Dependence on the Handpiece
steps.instructions: If the handpiece cannot be recognized or tuned during a procedure, stop using the affected handpiece. Maintain surgical continuity with an approved alternate method or verified replacement system. Do not repeatedly manipulate connectors while the system is being relied upon clinically. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely while the affected handpiece and console are isolated for troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the handpiece is not detected at all, is detected intermittently, begins tuning but fails, or had been functioning before becoming unavailable. Observe the console response during a controlled nonclinical connection and tuning attempt. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly categorized as recognition, intermittent connection, or tuning failure.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Handpiece Cable and Connector
steps.instructions: Power down or place the system in the appropriate nonactive state before handling connections. Inspect the handpiece cable, connector body, strain relief, and accessible contacts for damage, contamination, bending, moisture, or incomplete seating. Do not probe connector contacts with tools or attempt internal connector repair. Expected outcome: The cable and connector are clean, dry, undamaged, and fully seated. If reseating restores stable recognition and tuning, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Correct Handpiece and Accessory Combination
steps.instructions: Confirm the connected handpiece, tip, flue, cartridge, and other required disposable components are appropriate for the intended setup and installed in the correct configuration. Do not substitute components that are not approved for the system. Expected outcome: The handpiece and accessories form a compatible, complete setup.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Tip and Disposable Installation
steps.instructions: Examine the installed tip, flue, cartridge, and related external components for incorrect seating, looseness, visible deformation, contamination, or assembly errors that could interfere with tuning. Correct installation only using approved normal assembly methods. Expected outcome: All required disposable components are correctly installed and securely seated. If tuning succeeds afterward, perform functional verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Check for Moisture or Contamination at Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible handpiece and console connection areas for fluid, residue, or contamination. Follow approved cleaning and drying practices before retesting. Do not connect wet components. Expected outcome: All connection surfaces are clean and dry, ruling out contamination as the cause.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Handpiece When Available
steps.instructions: Using an approved known-good handpiece and appropriate accessories, repeat recognition and tuning. Compare the result without changing unrelated system configuration. Expected outcome: A known-good handpiece tunes successfully, identifying the original handpiece or its associated setup as the likely problem, or the failure follows the console and requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Known-Good Disposable Components
steps.instructions: If recognition occurs but tuning still fails, replace the applicable disposable components with verified compatible components when appropriate. Do not reuse suspect damaged disposables for repeated testing. Expected outcome: Tuning succeeds with known-good disposables, or the failure persists despite verified external components.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Once the handpiece is recognized and tuning completes, verify stable recognition, normal control response, appropriate irrigation and aspiration setup, and consistent nonclinical operation. Perform any required system checks before return to clinical use. Expected outcome: The handpiece remains recognized, tuning completes successfully, and the system functions normally. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Recognition or Tuning Failure
steps.instructions: If verified connections, correct assembly, known-good disposables, and an appropriate comparison handpiece do not resolve the problem, remove the affected component or console from service as indicated. Expected outcome: The unresolved fault is referred for qualified service-level evaluation without unnecessary internal repair attempts.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the CUSA Clarity handpiece was connected but would not complete tuning.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the handpiece connector was not fully seated at the console.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the connector, completed repeated successful tuning checks, verified normal system function, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the handpiece was recognized at all.
Results with a known-good compatible handpiece.
Whether the problem followed the handpiece or console.
Final tuning and functional test results.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Tip, Flue, or Cartridge Installation Problem
description: Addresses incorrect seating, assembly, compatibility, or damage involving the tip, flue, cartridge, or related disposable handpiece components.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Affected Setup From Use
steps.instructions: If incorrect disposable installation is suspected during surgery, stop use of the affected handpiece and maintain surgical continuity using an approved alternate method or replacement setup. Do not attempt to force, tighten, reposition, or disassemble components while the handpiece is actively being used on a patient. Expected outcome: The questionable handpiece setup is safely removed from clinical dependence.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Installation Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported issue is inability to install a component, loose fit, incomplete seating, repeated tuning failure after assembly, interference between components, leakage, or unexpected movement. Inspect the assembled handpiece externally. Expected outcome: The specific assembly problem is identified before components are changed.

steps.title: 3. Verify Component Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm the tip, flue, cartridge, handpiece, and associated disposables are intended for the CUSA Clarity configuration being used. Check packaging and labeling rather than relying on visual similarity alone. Expected outcome: All components are confirmed compatible. If an incorrect component is found, replace it with the correct approved component and proceed to verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Components Before Reassembly
steps.instructions: Remove the disposable components using normal approved methods and inspect for cracks, deformation, damaged threads or engagement surfaces, contamination, packaging damage, or signs that a component has already been compromised. Do not attempt to straighten or repair damaged single-use components. Expected outcome: Only undamaged, appropriate components are used for reassembly.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Handpiece Interface
steps.instructions: Examine the accessible handpiece mounting and connection surfaces for debris, residue, physical damage, or material left from a previous disposable setup. Clean only according to approved practices. Expected outcome: The handpiece interface is clean and free of obstructions that could prevent correct installation.

steps.title: 6. Reinstall Using the Approved Normal Assembly Method
steps.instructions: Install the required components in the correct order and orientation using the manufacturer-approved user-level assembly process. Do not force components or use improvised tools. Expected outcome: The tip, flue, cartridge, and related parts seat completely and securely without abnormal resistance.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good Disposable Components
steps.instructions: If installation still appears abnormal, replace the questionable component set with known-good compatible disposables. Avoid repeatedly reinstalling a visibly suspect component. Expected outcome: The known-good components install normally, identifying the original disposable as the cause, or the installation problem persists at the handpiece interface.

steps.title: 8. Confirm Handpiece Recognition and Tuning
steps.instructions: Reconnect the fully assembled handpiece and verify that the console recognizes it and that required tuning completes normally. Do not proceed to clinical use if tuning remains unreliable. Expected outcome: The assembled handpiece is recognized and tuning completes successfully.

steps.title: 9. Verify Irrigation, Aspiration, and Physical Stability
steps.instructions: Perform a controlled nonclinical functional check. Confirm irrigation and aspiration paths are correctly associated with the setup and that the disposable components remain securely positioned during operation. Expected outcome: Components remain stable and the system functions normally. Troubleshooting can stop once all required checks pass.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Installation Problems
steps.instructions: If compatible known-good components still will not install correctly, or the handpiece mounting interface appears damaged, stop further attempts. Expected outcome: The affected handpiece is removed from service for qualified evaluation rather than damaged by repeated forced assembly.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the CUSA Clarity handpiece could not be assembled because the flue would not seat correctly.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the disposable flue was visibly deformed and would not engage normally.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the damaged disposable with a compatible new component, verified proper assembly, successful tuning, and normal functional operation.

helpfulDetails: Exact component that would not install.
Irrigation and aspiration results after correction.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Irrigation Flow Low, Absent, or Inconsistent
description: Troubleshoots weak or missing irrigation caused by fluid supply, tubing, cartridge installation, clamps, kinks, connections, settings, or external flow obstruction.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Surgical Continuity
steps.instructions: If irrigation becomes unreliable during use, stop relying on the affected CUSA Clarity setup and provide an approved alternate method of irrigation or replacement system as directed by the surgical team. Do not continue tissue fragmentation with an irrigation problem that could compromise safe operation. Expected outcome: Patient care remains supported while the irrigation system is evaluated away from clinical dependence.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Irrigation Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether flow is completely absent, reduced, intermittent, delayed, or only affected at certain control settings. Observe the system during a controlled nonclinical irrigation test. Expected outcome: The exact irrigation behavior is reproduced and can be compared after each corrective action.

steps.title: 3. Verify Irrigation Fluid Supply
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct irrigation source is present, contains adequate fluid, is appropriately positioned, and is not empty, disconnected, or inadvertently closed. Inspect the fluid container and accessible supply connection. Expected outcome: A usable irrigation fluid source is present and properly connected. If restoring the supply corrects flow, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Entire External Irrigation Tubing Path
steps.instructions: Trace the tubing from the fluid source to the handpiece. Look for clamps left closed, kinks, compression, pinching under equipment, disconnections, incorrect routing, or visible blockage. Straighten or reconnect tubing using approved handling practices. Expected outcome: The tubing path is continuous, unobstructed, and correctly routed.

steps.title: 5. Verify Cartridge or Tubing Installation
steps.instructions: Confirm the irrigation cartridge or tubing segment is correctly installed in its designated external mechanism and fully seated. Do not force the cartridge or bypass interlocks. Expected outcome: The irrigation components are properly installed. If correcting installation restores steady flow, complete functional verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Check Handpiece-Side Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the distal irrigation connection and tubing near the handpiece for incomplete seating, leakage, kinking, or damage. Confirm the flue and related disposable setup are correctly assembled where relevant to the fluid path. Expected outcome: Irrigation reaches the handpiece through intact and correctly connected tubing.

steps.title: 7. Review Irrigation Controls and Settings
steps.instructions: Verify the selected irrigation setting is appropriate for the intended functional test and that staff have not inadvertently changed a control or preset. Do not alter protected service-level configuration. Expected outcome: Irrigation controls respond normally and commanded flow changes appropriately.

steps.title: 8. Substitute Known-Good Irrigation Consumables
steps.instructions: If the tubing or cartridge remains suspect, replace the applicable disposable set with a known-good compatible set. Repeat the irrigation test. Expected outcome: Flow returns to normal with the replacement consumable, identifying the original set as the cause, or the problem persists.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: With the complete setup assembled, verify continuous irrigation through the expected operating range used for functional testing and confirm there are no leaks, interruptions, or tubing movement. Also verify handpiece recognition and overall system readiness. Expected outcome: Irrigation is stable and repeatable. Troubleshooting can stop when required return-to-service checks pass.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Irrigation Failure
steps.instructions: If fluid supply, tubing, cartridge installation, connections, disposables, and settings are correct but irrigation remains unreliable, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The console or affected flow-control subsystem is referred for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported no irrigation flow from the CUSA Clarity handpiece during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the irrigation tubing was kinked where it passed through the equipment setup.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected the tubing routing, verified continuous irrigation and normal handpiece function, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether flow was low, absent, or intermittent.
Results with replacement tubing or cartridge.
Flow behavior before and after correction.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Aspiration Weak, Blocked, or Vacuum Unavailable
description: Addresses poor aspiration or loss of vacuum caused by tubing, collection components, connections, occlusion, setup, settings, or external vacuum-path problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Dependence on Unreliable Aspiration
steps.instructions: If aspiration becomes weak or unavailable during surgery, stop relying on the affected system and maintain suction using an approved alternate method or replacement CUSA setup. Do not continue using an unreliable aspiration pathway if it could impair visualization or surgical control. Expected outcome: The surgical team retains reliable suction while the affected system is removed from clinical dependence.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Aspiration Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether aspiration is absent, reduced, intermittent, noisy, or only weak under load. Ask whether the problem began suddenly or after a disposable change. Perform a controlled nonclinical aspiration check. Expected outcome: The reported symptom is reproduced and documented accurately.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Collection Container and External Vacuum Path
steps.instructions: Verify the collection container and associated connections are properly assembled, not full, not damaged, and correctly connected. Inspect accessible tubing for disconnection, collapse, leakage, cracks, or improper routing. Expected outcome: The collection and vacuum path are intact. If correcting a loose connection restores aspiration, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Trace the Aspiration Tubing to the Handpiece
steps.instructions: Follow the entire tubing path and look for kinks, clamps, compression points, blockage, or tubing trapped beneath equipment. Check connections at both ends for full engagement. Expected outcome: The aspiration tubing is continuous, open, and correctly connected.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Tip, Flue, and Handpiece Path for External Occlusion
steps.instructions: Check accessible disposable components for visible material, incorrect assembly, or obstruction. Replace contaminated or suspect single-use components rather than attempting inappropriate cleaning or clearing techniques. Do not insert tools into protected handpiece passages unless specifically authorized by manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: The disposable aspiration path is open and assembled correctly.

steps.title: 6. Verify Aspiration Controls and Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm the selected aspiration setting and any related controls are appropriate for the test being performed. Verify the footswitch or control input is commanding aspiration as expected. Expected outcome: The system receives the intended aspiration command and settings are not limiting function.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good Tubing and Collection Components
steps.instructions: If the external path appears intact but aspiration remains weak, install known-good compatible tubing or collection components as applicable. Repeat the functional test. Expected outcome: Aspiration returns with replacement consumables, identifying an external disposable problem, or the fault persists.

steps.title: 8. Compare Handpiece Setup
steps.instructions: If appropriate, test with a known-good compatible handpiece setup to determine whether the problem follows the original handpiece or remains with the console. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to either the handpiece/disposable path or the console-side aspiration system.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify stable aspiration during a controlled nonclinical test and confirm the tubing remains open, collection system remains sealed, and controls respond consistently. Verify irrigation and handpiece operation as appropriate before return to service. Expected outcome: Aspiration is strong, stable, and repeatable. Troubleshooting can stop after all required testing passes.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Vacuum Failure
steps.instructions: If the collection path, tubing, handpiece setup, disposables, connections, controls, and settings are correct but vacuum remains unavailable or weak, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is removed from service for qualified evaluation of the aspiration subsystem.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported weak aspiration from the CUSA Clarity handpiece during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the aspiration tubing partially collapsed where it was pinched beneath the console cart.
CCR.Resolution: Rerouted the tubing, verified stable aspiration and normal overall system function, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether aspiration was weak, absent, or intermittent.
Results with known-good consumables or handpiece.
Final aspiration and functional test results.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Handpiece Overheats or Stops During Use
description: Addresses handpiece heating or shutdown related to irrigation, installation, prolonged operation, cable condition, disposables, ventilation, or handpiece malfunction.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Immediately
steps.instructions: Stop using a handpiece that becomes unusually hot, repeatedly stops, smells abnormal, or behaves unpredictably. Move to an approved replacement handpiece or alternate surgical method. Do not continue operation to see whether the problem clears during patient use. Expected outcome: The patient is no longer exposed to an overheating or unreliable handpiece.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Ask whether the handpiece felt hot externally, stopped producing vibration, shut down after a period of use, or resumed after resting. Inspect the handpiece for discoloration, odor, damage, contamination, or evidence of fluid-related problems. Expected outcome: The failure pattern and any visible signs of overheating are documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify Irrigation Delivery
steps.instructions: Confirm adequate irrigation is reaching the handpiece. Check the fluid source, tubing, cartridge installation, clamps, kinks, and handpiece-side connections. Poor or absent irrigation must be corrected before further functional testing. Expected outcome: Irrigation is stable and appropriate for controlled testing. If restoring irrigation prevents heating and operation remains stable, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Tip, Flue, and Cartridge Installation
steps.instructions: Verify the disposable components are compatible and correctly installed. Look for misalignment, damaged components, obstruction, or incorrect seating that could contribute to abnormal handpiece operation. Expected outcome: The handpiece assembly is complete, correctly installed, and free of visible obstruction.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Handpiece Cable and Connector
steps.instructions: Check the cable, strain relief, and connector for damage, excessive bending, loose engagement, contamination, or heat-related discoloration. Do not use a handpiece with damaged insulation or connector components. Expected outcome: The cable and connector are intact and securely connected.

steps.title: 6. Check the Operating Environment
steps.instructions: Confirm the handpiece cable and console ventilation are not obstructed and that the handpiece is not being placed against heat-retaining materials during testing. Allow a handpiece that has become abnormally warm to cool before any bench evaluation. Expected outcome: Environmental factors are not contributing to excessive heat.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good Disposables
steps.instructions: Install a verified compatible disposable setup and repeat the nonclinical functional test while monitoring for abnormal warming or shutdown. Expected outcome: The problem disappears with replacement disposables or persists with the handpiece itself.

steps.title: 8. Compare With a Known-Good Handpiece
steps.instructions: If available, connect and tune a known-good compatible handpiece using the same verified console setup. Do not continue testing a handpiece that rapidly overheats. Expected outcome: A known-good handpiece operates normally, isolating the original handpiece, or the same behavior occurs and points toward a console-side problem.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: For any setup considered resolved, verify successful tuning, stable irrigation, aspiration, vibration output, and sustained nonclinical operation without abnormal warming, stopping, odor, or alarms. Expected outcome: The system remains stable during functional testing. Troubleshooting can stop only when abnormal heating does not recur.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Persistent Overheating
steps.instructions: A handpiece that repeatedly overheats, shuts down, or shows heat damage should not be returned to service based on temporary recovery. Expected outcome: The affected handpiece or console is removed from service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the CUSA Clarity handpiece became unusually warm and stopped during use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found irrigation flow was restricted by kinked tubing in the disposable setup.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced and rerouted the affected tubing, verified stable irrigation and sustained handpiece operation without abnormal heating, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the handpiece was hot, warm, or shut down.
Time or operating condition before the problem occurred.
Whether the issue followed the handpiece or console.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Footswitch Not Recognized or Pedal Functions Incorrectly
description: Troubleshoots footswitch detection, intermittent pedal response, or incorrect function caused by connections, cable damage, contamination, positioning, or control configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Prevent Unintended Activation
steps.instructions: If footswitch operation becomes unreliable during surgery, stop using the affected control and transition to a verified replacement system or approved alternate workflow. Ensure the footswitch is positioned where accidental pedal activation cannot occur during troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is protected from unintended or missing system activation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Footswitch Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the footswitch is not detected, a pedal does nothing, function is intermittent, the wrong function appears to activate, or the problem occurs only when the cable is moved. Test only in a controlled nonclinical condition. Expected outcome: The specific control failure is reproduced and understood.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Footswitch and Cable
steps.instructions: Examine the housing, pedals, cable, strain relief, and connector for cracks, cuts, crushing, fluid contamination, bent areas, or other visible damage. Do not use a footswitch with compromised cable insulation or significant fluid intrusion. Expected outcome: The footswitch is physically intact or a damaged accessory is identified and removed from service.

steps.title: 4. Verify Connector Seating
steps.instructions: Confirm the footswitch connector is attached to the correct console port and fully engaged. Disconnect and reconnect it using normal approved handling while the system is in an appropriate state. Expected outcome: The footswitch is recognized and remains connected. If reseating corrects the problem, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Connection Area for Contamination
steps.instructions: Check the footswitch connector and accessible console port for moisture, debris, or contamination. Do not connect wet components or probe contacts. Expected outcome: The interface is clean and dry.

steps.title: 6. Check Footswitch Position and Mechanical Movement
steps.instructions: Place the footswitch on a stable floor surface and verify each pedal moves freely without obstruction from drapes, cables, equipment wheels, or debris. Check that nothing is resting on a pedal. Expected outcome: Pedals move normally and cannot be unintentionally activated.

steps.title: 7. Review User-Level Control Assignment or Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm the console is in the intended operating configuration and that available user-level settings have not changed the expected pedal behavior. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or alter protected configuration. Expected outcome: Pedal behavior matches the selected normal operating configuration.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Footswitch
steps.instructions: If available, connect a verified compatible footswitch and repeat testing. Expected outcome: A known-good footswitch functions correctly, isolating the original footswitch, or the problem remains with the console-side interface.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify recognition at startup or connection, test each required pedal function in a controlled nonclinical setup, gently move the cable to check for intermittency, and confirm no unintended activation occurs. Expected outcome: All intended functions operate consistently and correctly. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Footswitch Interface Problems
steps.instructions: If known-good accessories, proper connections, settings, and physical inspection do not resolve the issue, remove the affected console or footswitch from service. Expected outcome: The unresolved problem is referred for qualified repair rather than bypassed.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the CUSA Clarity footswitch was intermittently not responding.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the footswitch connector was partially disengaged from the console.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the connector, verified all pedal functions repeatedly with cable movement, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Which pedal or function was affected.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Vibration Output Weak, Intermittent, or Unavailable
description: Addresses weak or missing ultrasonic output caused by handpiece setup, tuning, disposables, controls, connections, footswitch input, or external operating conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Using Unreliable Output
steps.instructions: If vibration output is weak, intermittent, or absent during clinical use, stop relying on the affected CUSA Clarity system. Provide an approved alternate surgical method or verified replacement system. Do not continue clinical use while repeatedly adjusting the system to compensate for unreliable output. Expected outcome: Patient care proceeds without dependence on uncertain ultrasonic output.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Output Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether vibration is completely absent, noticeably weak, intermittent, or lost only after a period of operation. Confirm whether the handpiece successfully tuned before the issue occurred. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly defined and reproducible during a controlled nonclinical test.

steps.title: 3. Verify Handpiece Recognition and Tuning
steps.instructions: Confirm the console consistently recognizes the handpiece and that tuning completes successfully. If tuning fails, address the recognition or tuning problem before evaluating output strength. Expected outcome: The handpiece is recognized and successfully tuned, or a tuning failure is identified as the primary issue.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Handpiece Connection and Cable
steps.instructions: Inspect the handpiece cable, strain relief, and console connection for damage, looseness, contamination, or movement-related intermittency. Reseat connections using normal approved practices. Expected outcome: The handpiece connection is secure and output does not change with normal cable positioning.

steps.title: 5. Verify Tip, Flue, and Cartridge Installation
steps.instructions: Confirm all required disposable components are compatible, correctly installed, and free from visible damage or obstruction. An incorrectly installed or damaged tip assembly can affect system behavior even when the handpiece is detected. Expected outcome: The complete handpiece assembly is correct and intact.

steps.title: 6. Verify Control Settings and Footswitch Command
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended output setting is selected and that the footswitch or other normal activation control is functioning correctly. Avoid changing service-level configuration. Expected outcome: The console receives a reliable activation command and the selected user-level settings are appropriate.

steps.title: 7. Confirm Irrigation and Aspiration Are Functioning
steps.instructions: Check that irrigation is available and aspiration pathways are not obstructed. Abnormal associated system conditions should be corrected before judging handpiece performance. Expected outcome: The supporting fluid and aspiration systems function normally.

steps.title: 8. Substitute Known-Good Disposables and Handpiece
steps.instructions: Replace suspect disposable components with known-good compatible components. If output remains abnormal, compare with a known-good handpiece when available. Expected outcome: The problem follows a specific handpiece or disposable component, or remains with the console.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify stable tuning and consistent activation during repeated nonclinical testing. Confirm output does not drop out with normal cable positioning and that irrigation, aspiration, and footswitch control remain stable. Expected outcome: Vibration output is stable and repeatable. Troubleshooting can stop when required verification is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Output Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good external components, proper tuning, settings, and controls do not restore reliable output, remove the affected equipment from service. Expected outcome: The system is referred for qualified evaluation of the ultrasonic drive or related internal systems.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported intermittent ultrasonic output from the CUSA Clarity handpiece.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the handpiece connector was loose and output dropped out when the cable moved.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the connector, verified successful tuning and repeated stable activation with cable movement, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether output was weak, absent, or intermittent.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Display, Touchscreen, or Settings Control Failure
description: Troubleshoots blank, frozen, inaccurate, or unresponsive display and control behavior caused by startup, contamination, accessories, settings, or external conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Using Unreliable Controls
steps.instructions: If the display or touchscreen becomes unreliable during surgery, stop depending on the affected console. Use a verified replacement system or approved alternate method. Do not continue clinical use when settings, status, alarms, or control selections cannot be reliably viewed or entered. Expected outcome: The patient is no longer dependent on a console with uncertain controls or display information.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Control Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the display is blank, frozen, intermittently responsive, inaccurate to touch, showing incomplete information, or responding slowly. Note whether physical controls still function and whether the console otherwise remains powered. Expected outcome: The display or control symptom is accurately defined.

steps.title: 3. Verify Normal Console Startup
steps.instructions: Restart the console in a controlled nonclinical environment and observe whether the display initializes normally. If the console itself fails startup, troubleshoot the power or startup problem rather than treating it solely as a touchscreen issue. Expected outcome: The console reaches its normal operating screen, or the broader startup failure is identified.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Screen and Accessible Controls
steps.instructions: Check for fluid, cleaning residue, adhesive film, debris, damage, cracks, or objects contacting the touchscreen. Clean and dry the display only according to approved practices. Expected outcome: The control surface is clean, dry, and unobstructed. If responsiveness returns, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Check for Glove, Draping, or External Contact Issues
steps.instructions: Ensure drapes, covers, cables, or stored items are not pressing against the screen or controls. During bench testing, use the touchscreen under normal intended conditions. Expected outcome: No external object is generating unintended or blocked inputs.

steps.title: 6. Disconnect Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Power down as appropriate and disconnect nonessential external accessories. Restart and reassess the display and controls. Expected outcome: The display functions normally with accessories removed, identifying an external interaction, or the control problem persists.

steps.title: 7. Review User-Level Settings Only
steps.instructions: Confirm the operating mode and visible user-level settings are appropriate and have not been inadvertently changed. Do not access restricted calibration, service, or hidden configuration menus. Expected outcome: Normal settings are available and respond correctly to user input.

steps.title: 8. Check for Intermittency
steps.instructions: Operate the console through normal nonclinical control selections and observe for freezing, delayed response, spontaneous activation, or failure after warming. An intermittent control fault is not considered resolved after one successful input. Expected outcome: The display and controls remain stable through repeated operation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify touchscreen response across the controls needed for normal operation, confirm displayed status corresponds to selected functions, and check alarms, handpiece recognition, and other relevant system responses. Expected outcome: Displayed information and control inputs are consistent and dependable. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Display or Control Failure
steps.instructions: If the screen remains blank, frozen, inaccurate, or intermittently unresponsive after external checks and normal restart, remove the console from service. Expected outcome: The console is referred for service-level evaluation rather than used with unreliable controls.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported the CUSA Clarity touchscreen was intermittently unresponsive during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried cleaning residue across the touchscreen surface that interfered with touch response.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned and dried the display according to approved practices, verified repeated touchscreen operation and normal system function, and returned the console to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the screen was blank, frozen, or inaccurate.
Presence of fluid or cleaning residue.
Final display and functional test results.

title: Integra LifeSciences CUSA Clarity Ultrasonic Surgical Aspirator - Repeated Alarm After Handpiece or Disposable Replacement
description: Addresses recurring alarms after component replacement caused by installation, compatibility, connections, tuning, fluid paths, consumables, or unresolved system conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Do Not Silence an Unresolved Condition
steps.instructions: If an alarm repeats after replacing a handpiece or disposable during surgery, stop relying on the affected setup until the alarm cause is understood. Maintain surgical continuity using a verified replacement system or approved alternate method. Do not repeatedly clear or silence the alarm while continuing use. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely and the repeated alarm is evaluated without clinical dependence.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Alarm Information
steps.instructions: Document the exact alarm wording or displayed message before changing additional components. Note whether the alarm appeared immediately after replacement, during tuning, upon activation, or after a period of use. Do not paraphrase the message in the service record when the exact wording is available. Expected outcome: The actual alarm condition and timing are captured for logical troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Replacement Component
steps.instructions: Confirm the replacement handpiece, tip, flue, cartridge, tubing, or other disposable is compatible with the CUSA Clarity setup being used. Check package labeling and component identity. Expected outcome: The replacement component is verified as appropriate. If an incompatible component was installed, replace it with the correct approved component.

steps.title: 4. Reinspect the Complete Installation
steps.instructions: Power down or place the console in the appropriate safe state and inspect all recently disturbed connections and components. Verify the handpiece connector, tip, flue, cartridge, irrigation tubing, aspiration tubing, and other affected external components are properly seated and routed. Expected outcome: All replaced or disturbed components are correctly installed.

steps.title: 5. Check for Packaging Damage, Contamination, or Defective Consumables
steps.instructions: Inspect the newly installed disposable for deformation, contamination, damaged connectors, compromised packaging, or other visible abnormalities. Replace any suspect disposable rather than repeatedly reinstalling it. Expected outcome: Only intact, clean, compatible components remain in the setup.

steps.title: 6. Verify Handpiece Recognition and Tuning
steps.instructions: Confirm the console recognizes the handpiece and completes tuning successfully. If recognition or tuning fails, address that condition before proceeding to broader alarm troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Handpiece recognition and tuning are stable, or the repeated alarm is traced to that part of the setup.

steps.title: 7. Verify Irrigation and Aspiration Paths
steps.instructions: Check that irrigation fluid is available and flowing, and that aspiration tubing and collection components are connected and unobstructed. A component replacement may disturb nearby tubing even when the replacement itself is correct. Expected outcome: Supporting fluid and vacuum pathways are intact.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Replacement Component
steps.instructions: If the alarm began immediately after installing a new disposable or handpiece, replace that component with another known-good compatible item when appropriate. Avoid changing multiple components at the same time unless necessary for safety. Expected outcome: The alarm clears with the known-good component, identifying the recently installed item or its setup as the likely cause, or the alarm persists.

steps.title: 9. Perform Controlled Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After the alarm condition clears, repeat tuning and perform a nonclinical functional check of vibration, irrigation, aspiration, footswitch response, and relevant controls. Confirm the alarm does not recur through repeated normal activation. Expected outcome: The system operates normally without repeated alarms. Troubleshooting can stop after required return-to-service checks pass.

steps.title: 10. Escalate a Repeated Alarm That Cannot Be Isolated
steps.instructions: If compatible known-good components, correct installation, stable tuning, and normal external fluid paths do not eliminate the alarm, stop further external troubleshooting. Do not continue replacing disposables indefinitely when the alarm consistently returns. Expected outcome: The console or affected reusable component is removed from service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: OR staff reported a repeated alarm immediately after replacing the CUSA Clarity disposable handpiece components.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the replacement cartridge was not fully seated in its normal installed position.
CCR.Resolution: Reinstalled the cartridge correctly, verified successful tuning and repeated operation without alarm recurrence, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Component replaced immediately before the alarm.
Whether the alarm recurred during final testing.
